newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paribas to sell Cr du Nord to SocGen.
newsitem.headline: Paribas to sell Cr du Nord to SocGen.

text.p: French financial holding company Paribas and bank Societe Generale said on Thursday they had approved the start of talks aimed at reaching a fast agreement on the sale of Credit du Nord by Paribas to Societe Generale for 2.2 billion francs.

The two companies said in a joint statement the transaction would take place in two stages. "During the first phase, Societe Generale would acquire a controlling interest in Credit du Nord and would make a commitment to acquire the remainder of the company's equity within the next three years," they said.

The initial acquisition by Societe Generale of a controlling share in Credit du Nord, giving it the majority of voting rights, would involve a 2.5 billion franc capital increase, reserved to Societe Generale, accompanied by a share purchase.

The capital rise would bring Credit du Nord's tier one capital ratio in line with Societe Generale's standards. For Paribas, the sale price of its Credit du Nord shares reflected the company's revised net asset value.
Societe Generale "should see continued positive trends in its 1996 financial ratio-- Cooke ratio, return on equity, net earnings per share -- following the acquisition," it said.

The statement said that the transaction enables Paribas to divest its retail banking activities in France to strengthen its focus on its two core businesses -- international investment and merchant banking and specialised financial services.
For Societe Generale, "the transaction offers a strategic fit with its objective of expanding retail banking operations in France."

For the Credit du Nord group, the support of a major retail bank will enable it to accelerate its development and improve profitability. The acquisition will also increase the size of the Societe Generale group in the French market.
Under the plan, Credit du Nord and Societe Generale will remain separate entities. Credit du Nord will coordinate activities with Societe Generale but keep its identity, franchise and brands.
Credit du Nord "has clearly confirmed its return to profitability, although its performance remains below that for equivalent activities at Societe Generale," the statement said.

Further profit improvement should come from pursuing current business development moves, developing new services with Societe Generale, productivity improvement and exploiting synergies with Societe Generale.
The implementation of a business plan should improve the profitability of all Societe Generale's retail bnaking activities, the statement added.
Existing partnerships between the Credit du Nord group and subsidiaries of Compagnie Bancaire will be pursued, the statement said.
